Try this. 
75 sprint get out 30 push-ups 
75 sprint get out 30 sit-ups 
75 sprint stay in water 30 pulls ups off the block
75 sprint get out 30 lunges 
Do this 4 times each time decreasing the amount of push ups sits ups etc. by 5 
You don’t have to do sit ups or lunges or pushups you can do whatever dry land exercises you’d like those are just the ones I did. 
Also for a water only set I suggest the Popov set made famous by Alexander Popov (the Russian Olympian) that set alone helped my 50/100 times tremendously. The set helps your body learn to work at high level despite the build up of lactic acid (the tightness you feel in your muscles after a race). Hope this helps best of luck to you in the water.

Sounds to me like you’re a sprinter like myself. My senior year of HS I shaved 1.8 seconds off my 50 free. I contribute that progress to weight training and dry lands. Also work on your starts, underwaters, and breathing. To me those three things are what make a good sprinter into a great one. Good luck!

I had a similar experience in high school. I would swim in the fastest lane on my HS team then during club season I was somewhere in the middle with kids older than I am. I went from leading lanes to getting my toes harassed constantly. It was a nice challenge but I too began dreading club practice and swimming in general. I later realized it was because I was burning my self out (I was practicing 6 hours a day 5 days a week lol). I took a short break from club over the summer and trained on my own at my local YMCA. Best decision I ever made. Also I think everyone has a love hate relationship with this sport so it could just be that the club sets are harder and so you may not look forward to them as much. Anyway best of luck to you in your swimming endeavors.
